purpose: Music selection, beat analysis, edit synchronization, track fitting, and dialogue-mix defaults.
principles: Choose music for emotional arc, groove, instrumentation, and structural fit before choosing it for BPM.
Use actual detected beat timestamps only for selected local sync points; use BPM only to describe tempo and create a fallback grid.
Treat beat, onset, downbeat, and section boundary as different event types.
Let story events, completed action, and intelligible speech override rigid beat synchronization.
Vary shot duration across half-beat, one-beat, two-beat, and phrase-length units.
Use strong effects and transitions on selected accents, not every beat.
Analyze the exact music excerpt used in the render because intros, live sections, and tempo changes can differ from the full-track estimate.
For music-led short videos, begin in or near a recognizable section and normally let a featured lift, impact, peak, vocal entrance, chorus, or drop arrive within two to five seconds.
Energy cannot identify cultural recognizability or lyric boundaries; verify known popular phrases with synced lyrics or auditioning, enter on the preceding beat, and end between complete phrases.
Shape the overall edit from musical sections and contrast rather than beat distance: readable setup, denser build, longer peak or payoff hold, and relaxed release.
Do not treat proximity to regular beats as an edit-quality score; viewers respond more strongly to hooks, section changes, contrast, and payoff.

eventModel.beats: Recurring pulse timestamps used as the basic rhythmic grid.
eventModel.downbeats: Likely first beat of a bar; preferred for reveals, new chapters, and major visual changes when confidence is sufficient.
eventModel.onsets: Local transient timestamps such as kicks, snares, notes, or impacts; preferred for precise accent cuts and sound effects.
eventModel.sections: Larger structural boundaries such as intro, verse, chorus, breakdown, bridge, and outro.
eventModel.energyCurve: Time-varying loudness or spectral energy used to shape escalation and select calmer dialogue regions.
eventModel.confidence: Analyzer-specific reliability measure. Low confidence triggers human review or a conservative fallback grid.

timingMath.warning: Do not extrapolate a full-track grid from one BPM value when actual detected beat timestamps are available.

initialSnapWindowsMs.note: Project tuning defaults, not universal perceptual thresholds.

cutSelectionPolicy.densityRule: Increase cut density for a musical build or action peak and decrease it for orientation, dialogue, and payoff holds.

analysisPipeline.name: decode-analysis-copy
analysisPipeline.action: Decode the selected excerpt to mono 44.1 kHz floating-point or PCM audio for analyzer compatibility. Keep the delivery master separate.

analysisPipeline.name: extract-rhythm
analysisPipeline.action: Estimate BPM and beat ticks. Store raw timestamps, confidence, analyzer name, version, parameters, and excerpt hash.

analysisPipeline.name: extract-onsets
analysisPipeline.action: Detect transient events and retain strength where the analyzer provides it. Remove events below silence or confidence thresholds.

analysisPipeline.name: derive-bars-and-phrases
analysisPipeline.action: Infer bar candidates only when meter/downbeat confidence is adequate. Otherwise expose beats without pretending that every fourth beat is a true downbeat.

analysisPipeline.name: estimate-energy
analysisPipeline.action: Measure short-window loudness/energy and onset density to identify calm, build, peak, and release regions.

analysisPipeline.name: validate-map
analysisPipeline.action: Reject non-increasing timestamps, merge duplicates within tolerance, inspect large interval outliers, and calculate drift against a tempo grid.

analysisPipeline.name: cache
analysisPipeline.action: Cache by audio content hash, excerpt start/end, analyzer version, and parameter set.

limitations: beat tracking can struggle with weak or changing pulse

strengths: confidence and interval outputs in RhythmExtractor2013
limitations: algorithm availability should be checked against the package build

fallbacks.condition: beat confidence is low but BPM is plausible
fallbacks.strategy: Create a tempo grid anchored to the first reliable onset; prefer two- or four-beat edits and avoid claiming downbeats.

fallbacks.condition: ambient or rubato track has no stable pulse
fallbacks.strategy: Use section, energy, and phrase changes with time-based shot ranges; do not force beat cuts.

fallbacks.condition: detected beat intervals contain isolated half-time or double-time errors
fallbacks.strategy: Normalize only clear outliers against neighboring median intervals while preserving genuine tempo changes.
Use a conservative 1.5-3.0 second shot-duration plan, align major moments manually, and mark the beat map as fallback.

musicProfiles.name: Uplifting Electronic
musicProfiles.editPattern: Establish on two- to four-beat shots, tighten to one beat in builds, and place the hero reveal on a phrase change or drop.

musicProfiles.name: Indie Pop Travel
musicProfiles.editPattern: Use longer phrase-aware shots than electronic music; emphasize lyric gaps, drum entrances, and chorus transitions.
avoid: using vocal-heavy section beneath dense speech

musicProfiles.name: Cinematic Build
musicProfiles.editPattern: Map story chapters to energy sections, use restrained cuts during the build, and reserve impact cuts for climaxes.
avoid: forcing a beat grid through ambient intro

musicProfiles.name: Driving Rock
musicProfiles.editPattern: Use kick/snare onsets for selected action cuts, preserve two- and four-beat road holds, and align destination reveals with chorus or riff changes.
avoid: burying engine accents under dense guitars

musicProfiles.name: Hip-hop Groove
musicProfiles.editPattern: Cut selectively to dominant drums, use held shots across sparse pockets, and treat double-time subdivisions as accents rather than the default cadence.

musicProfiles.name: Percussive Action
musicProfiles.editPattern: Use one- and two-beat action units, brief half-beat accents at the peak, and longer recovery shots after dense runs.

musicProfiles.name: Synthwave Drive
musicProfiles.editPattern: Use stable two- to four-beat movement shots, emphasize neon/city reveals at phrase changes, and avoid over-cutting sustained synth passages.

musicProfiles.name: Ambient Bed
musicProfiles.editPattern: Edit to speech, gesture, visual meaning, and energy changes rather than forcing beat synchronization.
avoid: music level that masks room tone or speech

musicProfiles.name: Lo-fi Groove
musicProfiles.editPattern: Use four- to eight-beat visual ideas, occasional snare-aligned B-roll changes, and subtle ducking.
avoid: using the loop as a reason for repetitive visuals

musicProfiles.name: Funk Groove
musicProfiles.editPattern: Use syncopated accents for cuts, pours, knife actions, and reactions while preserving longer shots between accents.
avoid: quantizing cuts only to quarter notes

videoTypeTempoGuidance.note: Slower cinematic tracks work when section energy is strong; faster tracks need longer beat groupings.
Pace can come from subdivisions and onset density, not BPM alone.
Maintain occasional four- or eight-beat road holds for spatial clarity.
Speech cadence governs the edit; instrumental density matters more than BPM.
Match groove and texture; preparation can be fast while hero food shots hold longer.
Use multiple cues appropriate to each chapter rather than one tempo for the entire video.

preferredOrder: Choose an excerpt whose natural section arc fits the target duration.
Start at a phrase or section boundary, not an arbitrary sample.
End after a cadence, impact, resolved phrase, or designed fade.
If shortening is required, remove complete bars or phrases from low-salience repeated regions.
Loop only an instrumental region with matching bar boundaries and a tested crossfade.
Time-stretch only for small corrections and only when artifacts are acceptable.
trackFitting.exactDurationRule: Trim or restructure the musical excerpt to the planned ending, apply a short fade when no natural ending exists, and use -shortest only as a final container guard rather than the edit decision.
trackFitting.loopRule: Loop on bar-aligned zero-crossing-friendly boundaries and audition the crossfade; do not loop vocals or evolving builds by default.

workflow: Clean and level dialogue before adding music.
Choose a sparse instrumental section under dense speech.
Use sidechain compression or timeline automation to lower music during speech.
Retain short ambience and action-sound windows where they add place or impact.
Apply final loudness normalization and peak control after mixing.

startingPoints.note: Creative starting ranges only. Tune threshold, ratio, attack, release, and gain from the actual voice and track.

popularTrackMetadata.policy: Popular music is accepted as a user-directed creative input. Metadata supports repeatability and does not block rendering.

supports: beat, tempo, and onset CLI capabilities
BPM, tick, confidence, estimate, beat-interval outputs and 44.1 kHz requirement
onset timestamp and onset-rate outputs and 44.1 kHz requirement
audio trim, fade, loop, tempo, sidechain compression, mixing, limiting, and loudness filters
